item: Herpes simplex infections of the mouth and lips (EDL)

symptoms: Acute, painful vesicular eruptions of the lips or ulcerations of the lips and mouth caused by Herpes simplex virus
Shallow, painful ulcers on the lips, gingiva, tongue and pharynx
Self-limiting infection with symptoms subsiding within 10 days

management_steps.details: Rinse mouth with homemade salt mouthwash for one minute twice daily (i.e. 1 1/2 medicine measure of table salt in a glass of lukewarm water). Ensure adequate hydration. Fluid diet for children. Avoid acidic drinks, e.g. orange juice or soft drinks, as they may cause pain.

Cover lesions on the lips with petroleum jelly. Pain: Children: Paracetamol, oral, 10-15 mg/kg/dose 6 hourly when required. See dosing table: Chapter 23. Adults: Paracetamol, oral, 500 mg to 1 g, 4 to 6 hourly as required (to a maximum of 4 g in 24 hours). Maximum dose: 15 mg/kg/dose. Extensive oral herpes (Children > 6 years and adults): Tetracaine 0.5%, topical, applied every 6 hours (apply thin layer on affected areas only, may be used inside mouth; note: safety in children < 6 years has not been established). Antiviral indication criteria: children with extensive oral herpes provided treatment started within 72 hours of symptom onset; PLHIV with herpes infections of lips or mouth. Children < 15 years: Aciclovir, oral, 250 mg/m2/dose, 8 hourly for 7 days. See dosing table, Chapter 23. Children >= 15 years and adults: Antiviral (active against herpes simplex) e.g., Aciclovir, oral, 400 mg, 8 hourly for 7 days.

warnings: Note: Safety of tetracaine in children < 6 years of age has not been established.
REFERRAL: Severe condition, dehydrated patients, no improvement after 1 week of treatment.
